Then do what the epic needs within the latitude contract: plan waves, dispatch one Commander per issue (each in an isolated worktree, each with a completed templates/LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md carrying pasted prior-wave verdicts, pre-rulings, honest-null clause, findings-file assignment, stop conditions, and inherited latitude), adjudicate what Commanders float (inside delegated classes as logged RULINGs, otherwise escalate), merge green reviewed PRs sequentially gated on check exit codes, and stop at wave checkpoints per the contract. Treat forecast as provisional. At every wave boundary or material exception, write .agent-work/epic-567-door/NEXT_WAVE.json with the exact boundary_id, launch_id, and trigger; consume exact ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json and ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_RESULT.template.json packets under .agent-work/epic-567-door/transitions/<boundary-id>/; append exactly one '- TRANSITION | boundary=<boundary-id> | decision=<decision> | verified' line to ADMIRAL_LOG.md; and run py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id epic-567-door in the foreground before any next launch. A nonzero result refuses launch. The verifier requires a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit, enforces repair safety, and writes CURRENT_TRUTH.md plus WAVE_REVIEW.md from revised_epic_body and wave_review_comment. Planning makes no direct gh/network mutation; future posting goes only through the authorized tracker port after normal gates. Log every ruling, incident, wave launch, transition exit, merge, and owned error in the ADMIRAL_LOG as it happens — an unlogged ruling didn't happen. Never run a Commander's issue yourself; never put two Commanders in one worktree. If the contract expires, a fixed-boundary proposal exceeds latitude, or the ground shifts under it, surface a contract-refresh or human decision before continuing.

closeout.title: Lessons audit, reconcile, hygiene, acceptance
closeout.imperative: The run cannot close without a record of what happened. 1) Write the epic retrospective as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened across the epic — not one per wave, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround, and each harvesting what the ADMIRAL_LOG, the crew Workflow Feedback and the Commander returns actually recorded. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/epic-567-door/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/epic-567-door/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-567-door --store-root episodes --phase feedback. 2) When any part of this closeout edits a shipped compact-format JSON template, edit the raw text surgically (never round-trip it through json.load/json.dump, which reflows the file and destroys blame) and re-validate with json.load afterward. 3) Hand the epic's net change to a constellation-cartographer subagent for architecture reconcile. 4) Hygiene: every branch merged or dispositioned, worktrees swept, ADMIRAL_LOG archived under .agent-work/archive/. 5) Present the epic summary and get user acceptance. Then release the lease: by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (your own spine; no session id argument needed). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id <admiral-session-id>.

why_trail.why: The epic's own defect blocked the run at step one: no verb binds the door to an existing spine, so the Admiral drove init on the CLI fallback. That makes #559 the anchor beyond argument and puts the doctrine sweep genuinely behind it -- you cannot delete a fallback that is currently the only path. Tommy signed a two-wave, seven-lane contract: W1 unblocks (A #559+bind-own-spine+#613, Opus; B #432; C #442+#595; G #574+#552), W2 subtracts. Merge and fix-now delegated; architecture surfaced; issue FILING held to closeout because tracking has been ballooning -- candidates stage locally and get paired onto open issues or recorded as episodes. Contract expires at the W1 checkpoint.

Wave 2 delivered the epic's outcome and it is verified on main, not asserted. origin/main at de8ef4ea runs 3374 passed / 6 skipped / 1219 subtests / 0 failed in a clean detached worktree, with the map index regenerated and passing; `git grep "CLI fallback"` over skills/, specs/ and the tracked .agent-work/templates/ overlay returns ZERO, and tests/test_cli_retirement_guard.py (718 lines) is on main to keep it that way. Five PRs merged — #627 F, #628 H, #629 D2, #630 E, #631 D1 — each gated on its exact head and main re-verified after every merge. The understanding that closes this step: #559's deliverable was never the deletion. D1 found that tests/test_mcp_adoption.py MANDATED the text across nine assertions, failing with "the CLI door must stay" — so every prior deletion was reverted by a red suite telling the deleter it had broken a rule. The regrowth was a mechanism, not drift, and it is now inverted, with the guard generalizing an in-tree precedent that already quoted the human. Two member issues turn out to rest on premises this epic's own measurements contradict (#442, #565), and both are escalated rather than closed because contradicting a human's written claim is not a delegated call.
